newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BSkyB sees no Oftel problems.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BSkyB sees no Oftel problems.

text.p: British Sky Broadcasting Plc is "confident" that its new interactive services project will not fall foul of telecoms regulator Oftel, deputy managing director David Chance said on Wednesday.
BSkyB is joining forces with British Telecommunications Plc, Midland Bank and Matsushita in a consortium to supply interactive services to TV viewers and subsidise set-top boxes.
"We've had many months of meetings with Oftel and we're confident they'll have a positive outlook on the project," Chance told Reuters.

Oftel is certain to look closely at the alliance between dominant telephone operator BT and pay television giant BSkyB. The two will each have a 32.5 percent stake in the new British Interactive Broadcasting consortium.
"The primary objective is to offer a wide range of interactive services...Everything from home shopping to home banking," said Chance.
BSkyB plans to launch its 200-channel digital satellite television venture in spring 1998. The interactive services will become available later that year.
"There has been huge interest from the content providers. The content providers have been banging down the doors to get involved," Chance said.
He added that the new consortium had been speaking to well over 50 companies who wanted to offer travel services, educational items and games.
BSkyB had originally planned to launch its digital satellite service this autumn but has now delayed it by some six months.
"If you look at the situation around Europe, a number of companies have rushed into digital with pretty mixed results," he added.
The consortium plans to subsidise the cost of set-top boxes down to around 200 stg, which Chance said would be "far, far cheaper" than in any other European nation.
Chance said the set-top box could, with an additional piece of equipment, receive digital terrestrial television (DTT) signals.
BSkyB, Granada and Carlton have joined forces to bid for three key DTT licences. The ITC is expected to award them by the end of June.
